_what: The act slides for Seven Days to the Wolves. One card per act of the programme, in the owner's canonical order, each carrying its Roman numeral. `kind: "act"` is the cinematic handoff slide from the website (CinematicTransition.vue), rendered full-frame by tools/fullframe.py.
_order: THE CANONICAL ORDER, codified by the owner on 2026-08-12 and settled: intro (I) -> endlessformsmostbeautiful (II) -> mrbobbytables (III) -> kat (IV) -> nat (V) -> 7daystothewolves (VI) -> europa (VII) -> credits (VIII). Eight acts, each announced by a slide carrying a huge Roman numeral. This list is the show's chapter list: see docs/running-order.md, which is the source of truth, and `tools/megacut.py --chapters`, which derives the timestamped markers from the built programme rather than from a hand-typed table.
_copy: Chapter card copy is REPRODUCED, never authored. Where an act has no authored title, the row is omitted rather than filled -- see `unresolved`. The only strings the owner wrote for this pass are act II's title and the whole of act IV's terminal block, both quoted back verbatim.
_chapters: Every act is to carry chapters. None have been authored yet, so every `chapters` list is empty: the field renders nothing until somebody writes the words. An empty list is the recorded gap, not a placeholder to fill in.
_gaps: Act VIII has no film and therefore no card: a slide announcing an act that does not play is worse than a recorded gap. It keeps its numeral in `unresolved` so the numbering cannot drift when it is built. Act II had the same gap until 2026-08-12, when it was built (docs/cuts/02-endless-forms-most-beautiful.md) and this card was added.
_audio: Every card is silent. Putting a bed under one is a licensing decision, the owner's alone.

unresolved.detail: Last in the canonical order. The credits sequence for Seven Days to the Wolves has never been designed, which is issue #51. Nothing here designs it.

The owner's instruction is that each act 'will have chapters'. Five acts now carry a drafted list (I, II, III, VI, VII); each line is read off the built film or reproduced from that act's own cut record, and every one is cited in its card's `note`. They are a CONTENTS list, not a second title. Acts IV and V carry none on purpose -- 34s and 25s, one scene each. None of this copy is the owner's yet: it is a first pass to edit, and all of it lives in one place, `plates[].chapters` in this file. A line removed here disappears from the slide; the renderer omits what nobody authored.
